blocks.title: Match OS to use
blocks.text: Embedded/real-time emphasise constraints; multi-user and distributed coordinate shared work.

blocks.title: Boot and control
blocks.text: BIOS/UEFI firmware begins startup; drivers provide hardware-specific access.

blocks.title: Virtualise
blocks.text: A hypervisor runs guest OSs; a language VM executes intermediate code.

blocks.title: Worked example · Model answer
blocks.text: A hard real-time operating system is suited because missing a deadline is unacceptable; deterministic scheduling/latency matters more than high average throughput. An embedded implementation may also apply. Check: link each claim to the scenario and use precise OCR terminology.

blocks.title: Shared worked answer
blocks.text: Use a VM with a hypervisor to run Linux as a guest OS, while a printer driver exposes the printer to the host OS or guest when assigned. Boot firmware starts hardware initialisation before the main OS loads.
